title: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
summary: A polyhex is an edge-connected set of n cells of the regular hexagonal tiling, where each cell has area one. We prove that the convex hull of a polyhex has area at most (1/6)*ceiling(n^2 + 14n/3), and we show that some polyhex reaches this bound for every n. This proves a conjecture of Kurz from 2008, which asked for the weaker bound (1/6)*floor(n^2 + 14n/3 + 1). The two bounds differ exactly when 3 divides n.
